name: App A2: AEP → MotionDoc converter for 2D films (keyframes, transform, shape, text, image, precomp, audio)
description: A pure converter in web/src/motion/aep/ that turns a director AepCompositionJson into a MotionDoc for the Motion engine: frame keyframes become seconds tweens with cubic eases, transforms map with pixel pivots, shape/text/image/precomp layers convert, audio becomes cues. 3D layers become warnings here (A3 converts them). Tested on every stored film.

readFirst: engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md (all except the 3D and Player sections)
one stored film: the newest data/films/*/versions/*.json
extraGuardrails: The converter is pure: no DOM, no fetch, no three. It imports only types and parse helpers from @engine/schema and @shared/aep.
manualGates: MG-1: owner opens http://localhost:5173/aep-motion.html?film=<id> for two stored films and compares them with the studio player.

stories.title: Keyframe helpers: frames to seconds, keyframes to tweens, bezier pair to cubic ease
stories.description: As a developer working on the converter, I want one tested function that turns an AEP property into a start value and tweens so that every layer kind animates the same way.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md sections 'Time' and 'Keyframes → tweens', shared/aep/transform.ts (keyframe shape: t, v, easeOut, easeIn) and engine/src/schema/parts.ts (Tween).

Create web/src/motion/aep/keyframes.ts exporting isKeyframed(value), easeFor(k0, k1): string ('none' or 'cubic(x1,y1,x2,y2)' with numbers rounded to 4 decimals), and propertyTweens(value, { fps, inPoint, props }) returning { initial, tweens } where props names the MotionDoc keys per component (e.g. ['x','y'] for position, ['alpha'] for opacity).
A vector keyframe splits into one tween per component in the same fromTo; at is clamped to ≥ 0; a zero-length pair is skipped.
Create web/src/motion/aep/keyframes.test.ts.
acceptance: propertyTweens([{t:0,v:0,easeOut:[0,0,0.58,1]},{t:18,v:1}], { fps: 30, inPoint: 0, props: ['alpha'] }) gives initial { alpha: 0 } and one tween { at: 0, duration: 0.6, from: { alpha: 0 }, to: { alpha: 1 }, ease: 'cubic(0,0,0.58,1)' }
A position pair [960,561.6] -> [960,563.76] over frames 0..120 at 30 fps gives one tween with from { x: 960, y: 561.6 }, to { x: 960, y: 563.76 }, duration 4
A constant 0.5 gives initial { alpha: 0.5 } and no tweens; three keyframes give two tweens back to back
With inPoint 30 a keyframe at t 45 starts the tween at 0.5 s

stories.title: Base transform and layer timing
stories.description: As a developer working on the converter, I want every AEP layer's transform, timing and blend mode mapped once so that each layer kind only adds its own fields.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Base transform' and engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts (LayerBaseShape including pivot from R7).

Create web/src/motion/aep/transform.ts exporting baseLayer(aepLayer, { fps, offsetFrames }) returning { id, start, end, x, y, pivot, scale, rotation, alpha, blendMode, tweens } using propertyTweens for position, scale (uniform when x = y in every keyframe, else scaleX/scaleY), rotation and opacity; unknown blend modes become 'normal' with a warning pushed to a passed warnings array.
Create web/src/motion/aep/transform.test.ts using a layer copied from a stored film.
acceptance: A layer with inPoint 0, outPoint 120 at 30 fps gives start 0 and end 4
transform { position: [960,540], anchor: [960,540], scale: [1,1], rotation: 0, opacity: 1 } gives x 960, y 540, pivot [960, 540], scale 1, rotation 0, alpha 1 and no tweens
A keyframed scale [0.9964,0.9964] -> [1.09604,1.09604] gives one tween on 'scale'; a non-uniform keyframed scale gives scaleX and scaleY
blendMode 'overlay' gives 'normal' and one warning naming the layer id

stories.title: Shape and image layers, and the asset table
stories.description: As a developer working on the converter, I want rectangles, ellipses and images converted with their assets so that backgrounds, cards and product photos appear.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Layers' and shared/aep/layer.ts (shape path, fill, stroke; image assetId) and shared/aep/asset.ts.

Create web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.ts exporting convertShape and convertImage, and web/src/motion/aep/assets.ts exporting convertAssets(comp, resolveUrl) mapping image assets to { type: 'image', url } and model assets to { type: 'gltf', url } (ids kept; MotionDoc ids must match its IdSchema, so map invalid ids through a stable sanitiser and keep the mapping).
Create web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.test.ts.
acceptance: The stored 'wake:bg' rect (size [1920,1080], fill '#F2E6CC') converts to a shape rect 1920x1080 fill '#F2E6CC' with pivot [960,540]
An image layer with assetId 'ast_87a5…' converts to an image layer whose asset exists in the converted assets with the asset's src as url
An asset id that fails the engine IdSchema is sanitised the same way everywhere it is referenced
Audio assets are not in the converted asset table

stories.title: Text layers with style and drop shadow
stories.description: As a developer working on the converter, I want headlines and prices converted with their font, size, weight, wrap and shadow so that titles read as designed.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Layers' (text row), shared/aep/layer.ts and shared/aep/effect.ts (text style and the drop-shadow effect) and engine/src/schema/layers2d.ts (TextStyleSchema).

Add convertText to web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.ts: style.font → fontFamily, size → fontSize (clamped to 4..512), weight → fontWeight string, fill, align, boxWidth → wordWrapWidth, lineHeight, letterSpacing, stroke; a 'drop-shadow' effect → style.dropShadow (distance, direction → angle, softness → blur, opacity → alpha, color); other effects → warning.
Add tests to web/src/motion/aep/layers2d.test.ts using the stored 'Slow mornings' text layer shape.
acceptance: { source: 'Slow mornings', style: { font: 'Inter, system-ui, sans-serif', size: 76, fill: '#ffffff', weight: 700, align: 'center', boxWidth: 1536 } } converts to text 'Slow mornings' with fontSize 76, fontWeight '700', align 'center', wordWrapWidth 1536
A drop-shadow effect { distance: 4, direction: 180, softness: 8, opacity: 0.35, color: '#000000' } becomes dropShadow { distance: 4, angle: 180, blur: 8, alpha: 0.35, color: '#000000' }
An unknown effect name adds one warning and does not throw

stories.title: Precomps to groups, layer order, audio cues, unsupported kinds
stories.description: As a developer working on the converter, I want scenes (precomps) nested as groups in the right draw order, with music as cues, so that a whole multi-scene film converts.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md 'Layers' (precomp, audio, video rows and the layer-order note) and shared/aep/composition.ts (precomps map).

Create web/src/motion/aep/convert.ts exporting convertLayers(layers, ctx) that reverses each list (AEP top first → MotionDoc back first), converts precomp layers into groups whose children are the precomp's converted layers (times relative to the precomp), collects audio layers into AudioCue[] with absolute seconds, and skips video, model3d, stage3d, actor3d and prop3d with one warning each (A3 converts them).
A group must have at least one child: an empty precomp is skipped with a warning.
Add web/src/motion/aep/convert.test.ts on a small hand-made composition with two precomps.
acceptance: A comp with layers [title, bg] gives MotionDoc layers [bg, title]
A precomp layer at inPoint 120 to 240 becomes a group with start 4 and end 8 and its children have start 0
An audio layer at frames 0..720 with level 0.7 becomes one cue { startSec: 0, endSec: 24, level: 0.7 }
A stage3d layer adds exactly one warning naming its id

stories.title: aepToMotion entry point and the stored-film golden test
stories.description: As a developer working on the player, I want one aepToMotion(comp) call that returns a valid MotionDoc for every stored film so that the swap can rely on it.
steps: Read engine/docs/10-aep-adapter.md (the signature at the top) and engine/src/schema/doc.ts (parseMotionDoc) and engine/src/timeline/targets.ts (validateTargets).

Create web/src/motion/aep/index.ts exporting aepToMotion(comp, opts) returning { doc, warnings, audio }: version 1, width/height/fps from the comp, duration = durationInFrames / fps, background = bgColor, assets, layers; the result is run through parseMotionDoc and validateTargets and any error becomes a thrown Error listing the paths (a converter bug, not a film problem).

Create web/src/motion/aep/films.test.ts that loads the newest version of every film under data/films (node:fs; skip when the folder is missing) and asserts aepToMotion succeeds for each, printing the warning counts per film.
Fix converter bugs the golden test finds; for a film feature that cannot be converted add a warning instead.
acceptance: aepToMotion on every stored film (newest version) returns a doc that parseMotionDoc accepts and validateTargets reports no errors for
The test prints one line per film with its layer count and warning count, and notes records the totals
aepToMotion never throws for unsupported layer kinds; it throws only when its own output fails parseMotionDoc

stories.title: Dev page: a stored film converted and played on the Motion engine
stories.description: As a project owner, I want /aep-motion.html?film=<id> to play a stored film on the new engine so that I can compare it with the studio player.
steps: Read engine/docs/06-runtime-player.md (MotionRuntime / MotionPlayer) and engine/src/react (the player component), and web/three-check.html with web/src/dev/three-check.tsx (the stub pattern).

Create web/aep-motion.html and web/src/dev/aep-motion.tsx: fetch /api/films/<id> (the composition of its head version, through the dev server's /api proxy), run aepToMotion, mount the engine's MotionPlayer, and show the warnings list, layer count and a seek slider.
If the engine's MotionPlayer does not exist yet (R4 not merged), write notes 'blocked: needs prd-r4-runtime' and leave the page showing the converted JSON and warnings only.
Open the page for the newest film in data/films with headless Chromium, save screenshots at 10 %, 50 % and 90 % to debug/app/ and record what you saw in notes.
acceptance: The page loads with no console errors and shows the warning count and layer count for the film
With MotionPlayer available, the screenshots at 10 %, 50 % and 90 % differ and show the film's background, text and images
notes names the film id used and the screenshot files
